speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
text: asked the Prime Minister with regard to the incident where almost 10,000 voters in Tanjong Pagar GRC received two poll cards (a) what lessons have been learnt; and (b) what measures will be implemented to prevent future errors.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: As a result, the affected households received duplicate poll cards.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: However, the duplicate poll cards showed the correct polling stations and the affected voters were able to vote at their assigned polling stations even if they missed the outreach by ELD on what to do with the duplicate poll cards.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: ELD will be instituting new measures to prevent such errors in future.

speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
text: This includes ensuring that the number of poll cards printed for a constituency is exactly the same as the number of registered voters in the constituency.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Ms Joan Pereira, keep your supplementary questions short.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: We are approaching the end of Question Time.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: And were there any voters who were unable to vote as a result of this issue?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: First, there is no change in the process.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: It is the same process by the same printer, done many times previously.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: How the mistake arose was that, in this particular time, they did not expunge the test data before they printed.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: So, we will work with the printer to make sure that we tighten this up.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The second point, in response to the question, while some of the affected households and voters received two poll cards, both poll cards showed the same polling station, which means that so long as the voter turned up at the same polling station, they would have no problem getting into the polling station to vote.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: What was different between the two poll cards for those affected is what we call the serial number.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The serial number does not determine whether a person can vote or not.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The NRIC or the passport, in this case, is the one that allows us to verify the person's identity to go inside to vote.

speaker: Mr Speaker
